text: Most AI courses spend three weeks on transformer math. You do not need it to ship an LLM system.
The model is the cheap, generic part. Your data is what makes the system useful.
If your AI feature is failing, ask: where is the data, when was it refreshed, who signed off on the shape. Almost always a data problem.

The bottleneck on building useful LLM systems is not the model. It is the data layer.

Production LLM systems that fail in 2026 fail at the data layer 9 times out of 10.

#building #ai #datafirst

Spend the first month on the data layer. Get one clean source flowing end to end. Validate the schema. Then bring the model in.

#building #ai #datafirst

A pattern I keep seeing: teams ship LLM features against three-month-stale data and wonder why production accuracy is 30 percent below demo.

It is almost never the model. It is the data layer.

The fix is unglamorous: one clean source, validated schema, refresh cadence. Then the model.

If the data is bad, the model papers over it. It hallucinates around the gaps. You do not catch the failure until a customer does.

This is the case for treating data work as the unblock, not the undignified.
